Pro Forma Large Load Cost Recovery Agreement

44.16.9 Appendix 9 to Attachment LL – Pro Forma Cost Recovery Agreement 
 
PRO FORMA LARGE LOAD COST RECOVERY AGREEMENT 
BETWEEN 
[NEW YORK TRANSMISSION OWNER] (Transmission Owner) 
AND 
[CUSTOMER NAME] (Customer)

TABLE OF CONTENTS 
Recitals and Regulatory Context 
Article 1: Definitions 
Article 2: Jurisdictional Harmonization 
Article 3: Scope and Construction of Network Upgrades and TO Attachment Facilities 
Article 4: Recovery of Network Upgrade and TO Attachment Facility Costs 
Article 5: Customer Payments 
Article 6: Financial Security, Creditworthiness, and Exit Protection 
Article 7: Breach, Default, and Remedies 
Article 8: Term and Termination 
Article 9: Miscellaneous and Regulatory Reservations 
• 
Appendix A: Description and Engineering Specifications of Network Upgrades and 
Transmission Owner Attachment Facilities 
• 
Appendix B: Revenue Requirement Breakdown 
• 
Appendix C: True-Up and Annual Revenue Crediting Accounting Protocols 
• 
Appendix D: Addresses for Notices and Billing

PRO FORMA LARGE LOAD COST RECOVERY AGREEMENT 
This PRO FORMA LARGE LOAD COST RECOVERY AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) 
is entered into as of this [___] day of [___], 20[__], by and between: 
• 
[NEW YORK TRANSMISSION OWNER] (“Transmission Owner” or “Connecting 
Transmission Owner” or “Affected Transmission Owner”), a [corporation] organized and 
existing under the laws of the State of New York, having an office and place of business 
at [___________]; and 
• 
[CUSTOMER NAME] (“Customer”), a [corporation / limited liability company] 
organized under the laws of the State of [______], having an office and place of business 
at [______], and owning a Large Load Facility with an expected peak demand of [__] 
MW at the Point of Interconnection. 
Transmission Owner and Customer are collectively referred to as the “Parties,” and each 
individually as a “Party.” 
RECITALS 
WHEREAS, Customer has submitted a Large Load Integration Request to interconnect or serve 
a Large Load Facility with an aggregate demand equal to or exceeding fifty megawatts (50 MW) 
[at a transmission-system interconnection point within the Transmission Owner’s service 
territory] or [affecting the Affected Transmission Owner’s transmission facilities in New York 
State]; 
WHEREAS, New York Independent System Operator, Inc. (“NYISO”) and/or Transmission 
Owner have performed system reliability impact studies, facility studies, and engineering 
assessments pursuant to the NYISO Open Access Transmission Tariff (“OATT”), identifying 
that the interconnection and commercial operation of Customer’s Large Load Facility will 
necessitate the construction and placement into service of certain Network Upgrades and/or TO 
Attachment Facilities on the [Transmission Owner’s] [Affected Transmission Owner’s] 
transmission system to maintain electric system reliability and system adequacy; and 
WHEREAS, Customer has received the cost allocation for Network Upgrades and/or TO 
Attachment Facilities identified by System Impact Studies and Facilities Studies under 
Attachment LL of the NYISO OATT or successor tariff provisions and has entered into, and 
posted Financial Security for the benefit of [Transmission Owner] [Affected Transmission 
Owner] in accordance with, the Large Load Security Agreement; 
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein 
contained, the Parties agree as follows: 
ARTICLE 1: DEFINITIONS 
Wherever used in this Agreement, capitalized terms not defined herein shall have the meanings 
assigned to them in the NYISO OATT or NYISO Market Services Tariff.

1.1 “Affiliate”: means, with respect to a person or entity, any other person or entity directly or 
indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under common control with such person or entity. 
“Control” means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct the management or 
policies of a person or entity; a voting interest of ten percent (10%) or more creates a rebuttable 
presumption of control.  
1.2 “Assessment Period”: A term of 15 years commencing on the Commencement Date. 
1.3 “Commercial Operation Date” (COD): The date on which Customer’s Large Load Facility 
has achieved energization and begins taking firm electric service pursuant to [the applicable 
Tariff] or [the Large Load Interconnection Agreement] at or above its designated minimum 
capacity commitment, as confirmed by notice delivered under the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement. 
1.4 “Commencement Date”: The date upon which the Network Upgrade and/or TO Attachment 
Facility is placed in service, as reflected in the In-Service Date under the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement [or other applicable agreement]. 
1.5 “Cure Date”: The last day of the applicable cure period under Section 7.2. 
1.6 “FERC”: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission or its regulatory successor. 
1.7 “Large Load Facility”: A newly interconnecting or expanded end-use electric load, co-
located arrangement, or data center facility with an anticipated peak electrical demand equal to 
or exceeding 50 MW connecting at a voltage of 69 kV or higher. 
1.8 “Large Load Upgrade Charge”: The monthly charge billed to Customer under Article 4 to 
recover the revenue requirement for the Network Upgrades and the TO Attachment Facilities 
specified in Appendix B. 
1.9 “Net Present Value Residual Charge”: A lump sum payment equal to the net present value 
of the Customer’s obligations under the remaining term of this Agreement at the time of 
termination that would have been collected over the remaining term of the Assessment Period, 
plus any cost of removal if applicable, calculated using the inputs set forth in Appendix B for 
each Identified Upgrade set forth in Appendix A. The discount rate shall be equal to the interest 
rate pursuant to Section 35.19a of FERC’s regulations, or successor regulation, effective at the 
time of termination. To the extent the calculation of the Net Present Value Residual Charge 
requires estimates of the Customer’s remaining obligations, such estimates shall be determined 
by the Transmission Owner in its reasonable discretion. 
1.10 “Network Upgrades”: Additions, modifications, enhancements, or replacements (other 
than TO Attachment Facilities) to the [Transmission Owner’s] [Affected Transmission Owner’s] 
electric transmission system required at or beyond the Point of Interconnection to accommodate 
the Customer’s Large Load Facility reliably under NERC, NPCC, NYSRC, and Transmission 
Owner [Affected Transmission Owner] reliability criteria and identified through the Large Load 
Integration Procedures contained at Attachment LL of the NYISO OATT and set forth in 
[Appendix A, the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, and/or other applicable agreement]. 
1.11 “NY PSC”: The New York State Public Service Commission or its regulatory successor. 
1.12 “Reimbursable Costs”: Costs and expenses incurred by the Transmission Owner in 
planning, designing, engineering, permitting, procuring, project managing, constructing, testing, 
and commissioning the Network Upgrades and the TO Attachment Facilities, including any

incremental costs resulting from a Customer-requested suspension or a Customer delay under 
Section 3.3, consistent with Good Utility Practice. 
1.13 “Related Agreements”: Collectively, this Agreement, the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement, the Large Load Security Agreement, and any other applicable agreement referenced 
in Section 3.4. 
1.14 “TO Attachment Facilities”: All facilities and equipment owned or controlled by 
Transmission Owner between the Point of Interconnection and the Point of Change of 
Ownership that are constructed or modified for the purpose of interconnecting the Large Load 
Facility, including line taps, breakers, disconnect switches, bus work, metering instrument 
transformers (if owned by Transmission Owner), System Protection Facilities at a Transmission 
Owner substation, and associated civil and structural works, as described in [Appendix A, the 
Large Load Interconnection Agreement, and/or other applicable agreement]. 
ARTICLE 2: JURISDICTIONAL HARMONIZATION 
2.1 Jurisdictional Harmonization. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as: 
(a) An assertion by the Parties of FERC jurisdiction over bundled retail transmission and 
distribution rates established by the NY PSC; or 
(b) A waiver by Transmission Owner or Customer of any rights, claims, or defenses 
under the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) or the New York Public Service Law concerning 
the jurisdictional boundary between wholesale and retail ratemaking. 
ARTICLE 3: SCOPE AND CONSTRUCTION OF NETWORK 
UPGRADES AND TO ATTACHMENT FACILITIES  
3.1 Identification of Upgrades. Transmission Owner shall engineer, design, procure, construct, 
install, commission, own, operate, and maintain the Network Upgrades and the TO Attachment 
Facilities detailed in Appendix A and the Large Load Interconnection Agreement, or other 
applicable agreement, which were, in turn, identified through the process contained within 
Attachment LL of the NYISO OATT. 
3.2 Milestones and Construction Schedule. Transmission Owner shall use commercially 
reasonable efforts to engineer, design, procure, and construct the Network Upgrades and the TO 
Attachment Facilities in accordance with the milestone schedule set forth in [the Large Load 
Interconnection Agreement and/or other applicable agreement]. All such milestones, other than 
the In-Service Date of the Network Upgrades and TO Attachment Facilities, are good faith 
estimates, and a change to any such milestone shall not require an amendment of this Agreement. 
Customer acknowledges that environmental review, Article VII and Article VIII permitting, and 
all property acquisitions are subject to New York State regulatory approvals and external 
contingencies. 
3.3 Suspension and Customer Delays. If Customer requests a suspension of construction or 
delays its commercial in-service milestone, Customer shall remain liable for all carrying costs, 
re-sequencing and re-mobilization costs, and cancellation fees incurred by Transmission Owner 
under Good Utility Practice during such suspension or delay. Transmission Owner reserves the

right to notify Customer if such suspension or delay is expected to increase the total estimated 
cost of the Network Upgrades or the TO Attachment Facilities and to require additional Financial 
Security in accordance with the Large Load Security Agreement. 
3.4 Related Agreements. This Agreement is entered into in connection with, and shall be read 
together with, [the Large Load Interconnection Agreement between Transmission Owner and 
Customer dated [●] (the “Large Load Interconnection Agreement”)] [and/or other applicable 
agreement] and the Large Load Security Agreement between Transmission Owner and Customer 
dated [●] (the “Large Load Security Agreement”). Customer shall be the same legal entity as the 
customer under the Large Load Interconnection Agreement (or other applicable agreement) and 
the Large Load Security Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this Agreement and 
any Related Agreement regarding the costs of, or charges for, the Network Upgrades or the TO 
Attachment Facilities, this Agreement shall control; and in the event of any conflict between this 
Agreement and any Related Agreement regarding Financial Security, the Large Load Security 
Agreement shall control. 
ARTICLE 4: RECOVERY OF NETWORK UPGRADE AND TO 
ATTACHMENT FACILITY COSTS 
4.1 Customer Responsibility for Allocated Network Upgrade and TO Attachment Facilities 
Revenue Requirement. Customer shall be responsible for and shall pay to the Transmission 
Owner the revenue requirement associated with the cost allocation to Customer for required 
Network Upgrades and TO Attachment Facilities identified in the Facilities Study specified at 
Section 44.12.1.8 of Attachment LL of the NYISO OATT, or successor provisions as set forth in 
Appendix A. The revenue requirement shall include, without limitation, appropriate depreciation 
or amortization, return, income and property taxes, operation and maintenance expenses, 
metering installation, administrative costs, and other costs as specified in Appendix B. The 
revenue requirement breakdown is specified herein at Appendix B. 
4.2 Large Load Upgrade Charge. The revenue requirement specified at Appendix B shall be 
recovered through a Large Load Upgrade Charge. This Agreement shall be specific to a single 
Large Load Facility, as determined by the Transmission Owner in its reasonable discretion. 
Transmission Owner shall calculate a separate charge for each Identified Upgrade (as defined in 
Appendix B) for which Customer is responsible, as set forth in Section 3 of Appendix B, and the 
monthly Large Load Upgrade Charge shall be the sum of all such Identified Upgrade-specific 
monthly charges. The monthly Large Load Upgrade Charge is specified at Section 4 of 
Appendix B for each month of years one (1) through the final year of the Assessment Period. 
The Transmission Owner shall follow the true-up procedures set forth in Section 6 of Appendix 
B. 
4.3 Early Termination. If, prior to the expiration of the Assessment Period, this Agreement is 
terminated, or Customer is in default under this Agreement or the Large Load Security 
Agreement and fails to timely cure the default, Customer shall be liable to the Transmission 
Owner for the Net Present Value Residual Charge, and the Transmission Owner shall be entitled 
to draw upon the Financial Security and apply it toward the Net Present Value Residual Charge. 
If any other outstanding charges or payments are due, Customer shall pay them within thirty (30) 
days of the termination date or the Cure Date, as applicable.

4.4 TO Attachment Facilities. Customer shall be responsible for and shall pay to the 
Transmission Owner (a) all actual costs incurred by Transmission Owner for studies, 
engineering, design, procurement, construction, oversight, testing, and commissioning of the TO 
Attachment Facilities, including applicable overheads, taxes, and line outage costs, to the extent 
not covered by any study cost reimbursement agreement or allocated otherwise under the NYISO 
OATT; and (b) Transmission Owner’s reasonable and prudent costs, including, without 
limitation, overheads, of operating, maintaining, repairing, and replacing the TO Attachment 
Facilities, except to the extent such costs are paid by a third party using such facilities. Unless 
otherwise agreed to by Transmission Owner and Customer in Section 7 of Appendix B, such 
costs shall be [included in the revenue requirement specified at Appendix B and recovered 
through the Large Load Upgrade Charge] [billed as a separately stated component of the Large 
Load Upgrade Charge] [, at Transmission Owner’s election, paid by Customer as a contribution 
in aid of construction in advance of or as incurred during construction], and Sections 4.3 and 6.2 
and Appendix C shall apply to the TO Attachment Facilities in the same manner as to the 
Network Upgrades. Customer’s responsibility for, and the recovery of, the costs of the TO 
Attachment Facilities shall be governed exclusively by this Agreement. 
ARTICLE 5: CUSTOMER PAYMENTS 
5.1 Commencement Date. Customer’s responsibility to make monthly payments shall begin as 
of the Commencement Date. 
5.2 Monthly Billing and Payments. The Large Load Upgrade Charge shall be billed monthly by 
Transmission Owner with Customer payment due within thirty (30) days. Monthly bills and 
payments shall be transmitted electronically in accordance with the information contained at 
Appendix D, or through paper copies, as the Parties may specify, using the addresses contained 
at Appendix D. The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to effectuate efficient billing and 
payment. 
5.3 Late Payments. Customer shall pay all invoices on or before their due date, regardless of 
whether Customer disputes the same in good faith. Any balances that remain unpaid when due 
shall accrue interest at the interest rate specified at 18 C.F.R. § 35.19a or successor regulation. 
Transmission Owner may include unpaid balances, with any accrued interest, on the next 
monthly bill. Any disputes shall be addressed in accordance with Section 9.11. 
ARTICLE 6: FINANCIAL SECURITY, CREDITWORTHINESS, 
AND EXIT PROTECTION 
6.1 Obligation to Post Financial Security. To protect other retail and wholesale customers 
against stranded asset risk in the event Customer fails to achieve the Commercial Operation 
Date, downscales its capacity requirements, or abandons installation of the Large Load Facility, 
Customer shall post and maintain security in favor of [Transmission Owner] [Affected 
Transmission Owner] in the amount and manner specified in the separate Large Load Security 
Agreement (“Financial Security”). Subject to the determination of obligations under Appendix B 
of this Agreement, nothing in this Agreement limits in any way the obligations of Customer 
under the Large Load Security Agreement.

6.2 Stranded Cost Recovery Upon Abandonment (Exit Protection). If Transmission Owner 
or Customer terminates this Agreement prematurely or otherwise defaults on its financial 
obligations: 
(a) To the extent that Transmission Owner determines within its reasonable discretion 
that the Network Upgrade is no longer needed, including based on written confirmation 
from NYISO that completion of the Network Upgrade is not required and that no other 
interconnection request, NYISO interconnection or transmission planning study 
(including any Reliability Needs Assessment or Short-Term Assessment of Reliability), 
or base case relies on completion of the Network Upgrade, Transmission Owner shall 
promptly cease incurring uncommitted costs and make reasonable efforts to mitigate 
losses, except in the case of actions necessary to preserve system reliability, avoid injury 
or loss of human life, or prevent environmental degradation. If NYISO informs 
Transmission Owner in writing that the Network Upgrade must be completed, 
Transmission Owner may continue to engineer, procure, and construct the Network 
Upgrade, and Customer shall remain responsible for all Reimbursable Costs of 
completing the Network Upgrade in accordance with Section 6.2(b). 
(b) Transmission Owner shall be entitled to draw upon the Financial Security as specified 
in the Large Load Security Agreement to recover all Reimbursable Costs, including 
without limitation engineering costs, committed equipment cancellation fees, 
environmental remediation costs, the costs to restore the bulk electric system to safe and 
reliable condition, including necessary expediting and acceleration fees, any non-
salvageable construction expenditures, the costs of removal, relocation, retirement, or 
other disposition of any facilities already installed, and, where the Network Upgrade 
remains needed under Section 6.2(a), the costs of completing the Network Upgrade. 
Customer shall remain liable for any such costs remaining unpaid after application of the 
Financial Security. 
(c) Any excess security remaining after full recovery and true-up shall be promptly 
refunded to Customer. 
6.3 Reduction in Maximum Load Facility Peak Demand. Any reduction of the Maximum 
Load Facility Peak Demand under Section 3.6 of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement 
shall not reduce the Large Load Upgrade Charge, the Net Present Value Residual Charge, or the 
Financial Security, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties. 
ARTICLE 7: BREACH, DEFAULT, AND REMEDIES 
7.1 Events of Default. An Event of Default shall occur if Customer: 
(a) Fails to pay any amount when due; 
(b) Fails to provide, maintain, renew, replace, or increase the Financial Security as 
required under Article 6 and the Large Load Security Agreement; 
(c) Becomes insolvent, files for bankruptcy, or undergoes dissolution; 
(d) Abandons or materially repudiates its development or interconnection obligations; or

(e) Is in default under the Large Load Interconnection Agreement (or other applicable 
agreement) or the Large Load Security Agreement and any applicable cure period 
thereunder has expired.  
7.2 Notice and Opportunity to Cure. Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, the non-
defaulting Party shall provide written notice. The defaulting Party shall have (i) five (5) Business 
Days after receipt of notice to cure any failure to pay any amount when due or to provide, 
maintain, renew, replace, or increase Financial Security, and (ii) thirty (30) days after receipt of 
notice to cure any other default that is capable of cure; provided that a cross-default under 
Section 7.1(e) shall arise only after expiration of the cure period in the applicable Related 
Agreement, and no additional cure period shall apply under this Agreement. 
7.3 Remedies. If an Event of Default is not remedied by the Cure Date, the non-defaulting Party 
may: 
(a) Terminate this Agreement upon written notice; 
(b) Draw upon the Financial Security to satisfy outstanding liabilities; 
(c) Suspend engineering, procurement, and construction of the Network Upgrades and the 
TO Attachment Facilities; and 
(d) Pursue any legal or equitable remedies available under New York State law or the 
FPA. 
ARTICLE 8: TERM AND TERMINATION 
8.1 Effective Date. This Agreement shall become effective upon execution by all Parties within 
the timeframe set forth in Attachment LL of the NYISO OATT[, subject to any filing with FERC 
that may be required under Section 205 of the FPA]. 
8.2 Term. This Agreement shall remain in full force and effect until all Large Load Upgrade 
Charge obligations and other payment obligations under Articles 4 and 5, including any Net 
Present Value Residual Charge, have been fully satisfied. 
8.3 Regulatory Modification. Without creating any additional regulatory filing obligations, if 
FERC or the NY PSC issues an order requiring a material modification, including termination or 
rejection, of this Agreement, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith for sixty (60) days to 
conform the Agreement. If agreement cannot be reached, Transmission Owner may terminate 
this Agreement and draw upon the Financial Security for all incurred, unrecoverable 
Reimbursable Costs.  
8.4 Cross-Termination. Termination of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement (or other 
applicable agreement) for any reason other than Transmission Owner’s Default (including 
Customer’s termination for convenience or non-renewal) shall constitute early termination of this 
Agreement for purposes of Section 4.3, and the Net Present Value Residual Charge shall become 
due. 
ARTICLE 9: MISCELLANEOUS AND REGULATORY 
RESERVATIONS

9.1 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by, construed, and enforced in 
accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of law 
principles, except to the extent that matters fall within the exclusive jurisdiction of FERC, the 
FPA, or federal common law. 
9.2 FPA Sections 205 and 206 Reservations. Nothing contained in this Agreement shall limit 
the statutory right of Transmission Owner to unilaterally file with FERC, under Section 205 of 
the FPA and FERC’s regulations, for modifications in rates, charges, classifications, or terms of 
service; nor shall it restrict the rights of Customer or the NY PSC under Section 206 of the FPA. 
9.3 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by 
a court or regulatory agency of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall continue in 
full force, provided the core economic and jurisdictional balance intended by the Parties remains 
intact. 
9.4 Execution in Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in two or more counterparts, 
each of which shall be deemed an original, but all of which together shall constitute one and the 
same instrument. 
9.5 Notice. Unless otherwise provided in this Agreement, any required notice shall be made in 
writing, and shall be effective when delivered by recognized national courier, certified or 
registered mail, personal delivery, electronic mail, or another method permitted by this 
Agreement, addressed to the Party at the address set forth in Appendix D. 
9.6 Amendment; Waiver. This Agreement may be amended, superseded, or modified by a 
written instrument executed by both Parties, subject to any required filing with and acceptance 
by FERC and any required approval of the NY PSC. No waiver shall be effective unless in 
writing and signed by the Party against whom it is sought to be enforced. The failure of a Party 
to insist on strict performance on any occasion shall not be a waiver, and no waiver of any 
breach shall be a continuing waiver or a waiver of any other or subsequent breach. 
9.7 Assignment. No Party may assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the 
other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided 
that Transmission Owner may assign this Agreement on notice, without consent, to an Affiliate 
or in connection with a sale, merger, restructuring, or transfer of all or substantially all of its 
assets, so long as the assignee assumes in writing all rights and obligations under this 
Agreement. Any assignment by Customer (other than a collateral assignment) and any change of 
control of Customer shall require Transmission Owner’s prior written consent, not to be 
unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and shall be conditioned on (i) the assignee 
assuming in writing all obligations under this Agreement, the Large Load Interconnection 
Agreement, and the Large Load Security Agreement, each of which shall be assigned to the same 
assignee at the same time; and (ii) Customer reimbursing Transmission Owner’s reasonable costs 
of administering the assignment or performing due diligence with respect to a change of control. 
Customer may assign this Agreement on notice, without consent, as collateral security in 
connection with financing of the Large Load Facility. Any assignment in violation of this 
Section is void. No assignment relieves the assigning Party of its obligations. No assignment 
shall be effective unless the assignee provides and maintains Financial Security satisfying the 
requirements of Article 6 and the Large Load Security Agreement, and no assignment by 
Customer shall release Customer or any existing Financial Security until the assignee’s 
replacement Financial Security has been posted and accepted.

9.8 Limitation of Liability. In no event, whether as a result of breach of contract, tort (including 
negligence and strict liability), or otherwise, shall any Party be liable in connection with this 
Agreement for any special, indirect, incidental, penal, punitive, or consequential damages of any 
nature, including delays, lost profits, business interruptions, and claims of suppliers and 
customers, whether or not such damages were reasonably foreseeable or such Party was advised 
that such damages might be incurred; provided that this Section shall not limit Customer’s 
obligation to pay the Large Load Upgrade Charge, the Net Present Value Residual Charge, costs 
recoverable under Sections 3.3, 4.3, 6.2, and 8.3, or other amounts due under this Agreement. 
TRANSMISSION OWNER MAKES NO WARRANTIES, REPRESENTATIONS, OR 
GUARANTEES IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, THE NETWORK 
UPGRADES, THE TO ATTACHMENT FACILITIES, OR ANY WORK PERFORMED BY 
TRANSMISSION OWNER, WHETHER WRITTEN OR ORAL, STATUTORY, EXPRESS OR 
IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF 
MERCHANTABILITY AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, ALL OF WHICH 
ARE HEREBY EXPRESSLY EXCLUDED AND DISCLAIMED. 
9.9 Force Majeure. No Party shall be considered in default of any obligation under this 
Agreement to the extent its performance is prevented or delayed by an event of Force 
Majeure, provided that such Party gives prompt written notice and uses reasonable efforts to 
resume performance. “Force Majeure” means any act of God, labor disturbance, act of the 
public enemy, war, terrorism, insurrection, riot, fire, storm, flood or other unusually severe 
weather, earthquake, epidemic, explosion, breakage or accident to machinery or equipment, 
any order, regulation, or restriction imposed by a governmental, military, or lawfully 
established civilian authority (including any delay by a governmental authority), or any other 
cause beyond the reasonable control of the Party claiming Force Majeure. Force Majeure 
does not include acts of negligence or intentional wrongdoing by the Party claiming Force 
Majeure, or the lack of funds or financing. Force Majeure shall not include, with respect to 
Customer: (a) economic hardship, changes in market conditions, or the cost or unavailability 
of financing; (b) delays in Customer’s procurement of equipment or failure of Customer’s 
suppliers or contractors, unless caused by an independent Force Majeure event; (c) labor 
disputes involving only Customer’s or its contractors’ workforce; (d) Customer’s failure to 
obtain required permits or approvals, unless it has diligently and timely pursued them; or (e) 
changes in the demand for, or the business case of, the Large Load Facility’s end use. Force 
Majeure shall not excuse any obligation to make payments or to post and maintain Financial 
Security. 
9.10 
Effect of Force Majeure. A Party shall be excused from performance (other than the 
obligation to pay money when due or to timely post and maintain Financial Security) to the 
extent prevented by Force Majeure, provided it gives prompt notice with full particulars 
(confirming any telephone notice in writing), keeps the other Party informed, and exercises 
due diligence to remedy the effects with reasonable dispatch. A Party shall not be required to 
settle a labor dispute on terms unsatisfactory to it. 
9.11 Dispute Resolution. 
(a) Notice and Informal Resolution. A Party asserting a dispute arising out of or relating 
to this Agreement (a “Dispute”) shall give written notice (a “Notice of Dispute”). The 
Dispute shall be referred to designated senior representatives of the Parties for good-faith 
negotiation.

(b) Arbitration by Agreement. If the Dispute is not resolved within [thirty (30) / sixty 
(60)] days after receipt of the Notice of Dispute, the Parties may, by mutual agreement, 
submit it to arbitration under Section 9.11(c). Absent such agreement, either Party may 
pursue any remedy available at law or in equity, including proceedings before FERC, the 
NY PSC, or a court of competent jurisdiction. Any court proceeding arising out of or 
relating to this Agreement shall be brought exclusively in the courts identified in Section 
14.3 of the Large Load Interconnection Agreement. EACH PARTY KNOWINGLY, 
VOLUNTARILY, AND IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY 
OF ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, TO 
THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW. Notwithstanding this 
Section 9.11, (i) either Party may at any time seek temporary, preliminary, or injunctive 
relief, or specific performance, from a court of competent jurisdiction or from FERC or the 
NY PSC to prevent irreparable harm, protect system reliability or safety, or preserve the 
status quo, without first complying with Section 9.11(a); and (ii) the informal resolution 
and arbitration procedures shall not delay or limit Transmission Owner’s exercise of its 
rights under Article 6, Section 7.3, and Section 8.3, or Customer’s payment obligations 
under Article 5 or its obligation to provide and maintain Financial Security under Article 
6 and the Large Load Security Agreement. 
(c) Arbitration Procedures. Any arbitration shall be conducted before a single neutral 
arbitrator, or, if the Parties cannot agree on one within ten (10) days, a three-member panel 
(one appointed by each Party and a third selected by the two party-appointed arbitrators), 
each knowledgeable in electric utility matters and without substantial business 
relationships with either Party, under the Commercial Arbitration Rules of the American 
Arbitration Association, except as modified herein. The arbitrator(s) shall render a written, 
reasoned decision within ninety (90) days of appointment, shall have no authority to 
modify this Agreement, and the decision shall be final, with judgment enterable in any 
court of competent jurisdiction, subject to appeal only on grounds permitted by the Federal 
Arbitration Act. Each Party shall bear its own costs, the cost of its appointed arbitrator, and 
one-half of the cost of the single or third arbitrator. 
(d) Continued Performance; Termination. Pending resolution, each Party shall continue 
to perform its obligations, including by paying disputed amounts, and Customer shall 
continue to provide and maintain Financial Security as required under Article 6 and the 
Large Load Security Agreement. The pendency of a Dispute shall not suspend or toll any 
cure period under Article 7 or limit Transmission Owner’s rights described in Section 
9.11(b)(ii). Whether a termination is proper shall not be subject to arbitration unless the 
Parties agree otherwise. 
9.12 Confidentiality. Subject to any reporting or posting obligations under the NYISO OATT 
and any directives or requirements of FERC, the NY PSC, or NYISO, information exchanged 
under this Agreement that is designated confidential by the disclosing Party, including Critical 
Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information, shall be held in confidence and used only for 
purposes of this Agreement, subject to the confidentiality provisions of the NYISO OATT, 
applicable laws and regulations, and any non-disclosure agreements between the Parties; 
provided that nothing in this Section shall restrict the disclosure of cost information required 
under the NYISO OATT or any filing with FERC or the NY PSC. Critical Energy/Electric 
Infrastructure Information shall be protected and disclosed only as permitted by 18 C.F.R. §

388.113, the NYISO OATT, applicable NYISO procedures, and any FERC order. Transmission 
Owner may require Customer and its contractors, subcontractors, vendors, or agents to execute a 
separate non-disclosure agreement as a condition of receiving confidential information or 
Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information, and nothing in this Agreement shall limit, 
modify, or supersede any such non-disclosure agreement. 
9.13 Representations and Warranties. As of the date of execution, each Party represents and 
warrants to the other Party that: (i) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing 
under the laws of its jurisdiction of formation; (ii) it has all regulatory authorizations necessary 
to perform its obligations under this Agreement, other than any FERC [or NY PSC] acceptance 
that may be required; (iii) its execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement are within 
its powers, have been duly authorized, and do not violate its governing documents or, in any

2. Defined Terms and Variables 
For purposes of this Appendix B, the following terms and variables shall have the meanings set 
forth below. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Appendix B shall have the meanings 
set forth in Article 1 of the Agreement. 
(a) [“Annual Deferred Revenue” means, for each Billing Year, the amount by which the 
Estimated Accelerated Annual Revenue Requirement exceeds the Estimated Annual 
Revenue Requirement for such Billing Year.]

(b) “Annual On-going Charge Factor” or “OCF” means the annual percentage calculated 
by dividing the Transmission Owner’s applicable transmission and distribution 
operations and maintenance expenses, administrative and general expenses, property 
taxes, payroll taxes, and other applicable expenses, excluding depreciation and 
amortization expense, return on investment, and associated income taxes, by the 
Transmission Owner’s total transmission and distribution gross plant in service for the 
applicable period. 
(c) “Average Service Life” or “ASL” means the dollar weighted average composite 
service life, expressed in years, of the property units comprising the Identified Upgrade, 
determined by weighting the service life associated with the depreciation rate approved 
for the Transmission Owner for each applicable plant account by the portion of the 
Estimated Network Upgrade Book Value recorded to that plant account, consistent with 
Section 3 of this Appendix B. 
(d) “Billing Year” means each consecutive twelve (12) month period during the 
Assessment Period, the first of which shall commence on the Commencement Date and 
each subsequent one of which shall commence on the anniversary of the 
Commencement Date. 
(e) “Contract Term” or “CT” means the number of years in the Assessment Period, as 
specified in Section 1.2 of the Agreement. 
(f) “Estimated Accelerated Annual Revenue Requirement” or “EAARR” means, for 
each Billing Year, the annual revenue requirement payable by Customer under this 
Agreement, determined in accordance with Section 3(e) of this Appendix B. 
(g) “Estimated Annual Revenue Requirement” or “EARR” means, for each Billing 
Year, the estimated annual revenue requirement associated with the Estimated Network 
Upgrade Book Value, determined in accordance with Section 3(c) of this Appendix B. 
(h) “Estimated Network Upgrade Book Value” or “ENUBV” means, for each Identified 
Upgrade, the Total Estimated Capital Cost set forth in Section 1 of this Appendix B, as 
such amount will be replaced by actual Reimbursable Costs in accordance with Section 
6(c) of this Appendix B and adjusted annually for deduction of accumulated 
depreciation and amortization. 
(i) “Identified Upgrade” means each Network Upgrade and each TO Attachment Facility 
for which Customer is responsible, in whole or in an allocated share, as identified in 
the applicable Facilities Study and set forth in a table in Section 1 of this Appendix B. 
An Identified Upgrade may consist of more than one component. 
(j) “Large Load Upgrade Gross Plant in Service” or “LLGP” means the capital cost of 
the Identified Upgrade in service allocated to Customer under this Agreement, initially 
estimated and subsequently replaced by actual Reimbursable Costs under Section 6(c) 
of this Appendix B, before deduction of accumulated depreciation and amortization. 
(k) “Large Load Upgrade-Specific Capital Revenue Requirement” or “LLCRR” 
means, for each Billing Year, the sum of (i) depreciation and amortization expense 
attributable to the Identified Upgrade, calculated using the applicable approved 
depreciation and amortization rates, and (ii) the authorized return on the Identified 
Upgrade-specific investment balance, including associated income taxes. The

investment balance used to calculate return shall reflect accumulated depreciation and 
amortization and any other applicable rate-base adjustments specified in this 
Agreement. This amount excludes expenses recovered through the Annual On-going 
Charge Factor. 
(l) “Rate Data Sources” has the meaning set forth in Section 5(b) of this Appendix B. 
(m) “T/D” means the transmission and distribution functions of the Transmission Owner’s 
electric utility operations, as such functions are classified and functionalized in the Rate 
Data Sources. 
(n) “Total T/D Investment Base” has the meaning set forth in Section 5(d) of this 
Appendix B. 
(o) “Total T/D Plant” or “TTDP” has the meaning set forth in Section 5(c) of this 
Appendix B. 
(p) “Total T/D Revenue Requirements Allocable” or “TRRA” has the meaning set forth 
in Section 5(e) of this Appendix B. 
3. Calculation of the Estimated Accelerated Annual Revenue Requirement 
For each Billing Year during the Assessment Period, Transmission Owner shall calculate the 
Estimated Accelerated Annual Revenue Requirement, which shall constitute the annual Large 
Load Upgrade Charge, by performing the following steps in sequence: 
(a) Step One – Estimated Network Upgrade Book Value. Transmission Owner shall 
determine the Estimated Network Upgrade Book Value for each Identified Upgrade, which 
shall equal the total estimated capital cost of such Identified Upgrade, inclusive of direct 
costs, applicable indirect costs (including overheads and allowance for funds used during 
construction (“AFUDC”)), as set forth in Section 1 of this Appendix B and as recorded in 
accordance with FERC’s Uniform System of Accounts, 18 C.F.R. Part 101. 
(b) Step Two – Annual On-going Charge Factor and Large Load Upgrade-Specific 
Capital Revenue Requirement. Transmission Owner shall determine the Annual On-
going Charge Factor in effect for the Billing Year in accordance with Sections 5 and 6 of 
this Appendix B. Transmission Owner shall also determine the LLCRR for the applicable 
Billing Year using the applicable approved inputs and Identified Upgrade-specific 
investment balances. 
(c) Step Three – Estimated Annual Revenue Requirement. Transmission Owner shall 
add the LLCRR to the product of the Large Load Upgrade Gross Plant in Service and the 
Annual On-going Charge Factor, and round the sum to the nearest [rounding increment to 
be specified by Transmission Owner], as follows: 
EARR = LLCRR + (LLGP × OCF) 
The Estimated Annual Revenue Requirement represents the estimated annual cost of 
owning, operating, and maintaining the Identified Upgrade. 
(d) Step Four – Average Service Life and Contract Term. Transmission Owner shall 
determine the Average Service Life of the Identified Upgrade and the Contract Term, each

expressed in years, in accordance with the definitions set forth in Section 2 of this Appendix 
B. 
(e) Step Five – Estimated Accelerated Annual Revenue Requirement. Transmission 
Owner shall multiply the Estimated Annual Revenue Requirement by the Average Service 
Life and divide the product by the Contract Term, as follows: 
EAARR = (EARR × ASL) ÷ CT 
The resulting Estimated Accelerated Annual Revenue Requirement provides for the 
recovery within the Contract Term of the aggregate Estimated Annual Revenue 
Requirements that would otherwise be recovered over the Average Service Life of the 
Identified Upgrade. 
(f) Annual and Monthly Large Load Upgrade Charge. Transmission Owner shall 
perform the calculation set forth in this Section 3 separately for each Identified Upgrade. 
The annual Large Load Upgrade Charge for each Billing Year shall equal the sum of the 
Estimated Accelerated Annual Revenue Requirements for all Identified Upgrades for that 
Billing Year. The monthly Large Load Upgrade Charge shall equal one-twelfth of the 
annual Large Load Upgrade Charge, as set forth in Section 4 of this Appendix B.

5. Annual On-going Charge Factor: Methodology and Input Data Sources 
(a) Formula. The Annual On-going Charge Factor shall equal the Total T/D Revenue 
Requirements Allocable divided by the Total T/D Plant, as follows: 
OCF = TRRA ÷ TTDP 
For purposes of calculating the OCF, the TRRA used in the numerator shall exclude 
depreciation and amortization expense, return on investment, and associated income 
taxes, and TTDP represents total transmission and distribution gross plant in service. 
(b) Rate Data Sources. Each input to the Annual On-going Charge Factor shall be derived 
exclusively from the following sources (collectively, the “Rate Data Sources”), each as 
in effect or as most recently filed with, or issued or approved by, the NY PSC as of the date 
of the applicable annual update: 
(i) the revenue requirement, rate base, depreciation rates, capital structure, cost of 
capital, return on common equity, and functionalization and allocation

methodologies established in or approved pursuant to Transmission Owner’s most 
recent electric rate order issued by the NY PSC [in Case No. ______], including 
any joint proposal or multi-year rate plan adopted therein (the “NY PSC Rate 
Order”), applied to both the transmission and distribution functions comprising 
T/D; 
(ii) Transmission Owner’s annual report filed with the NY PSC, and any 
compliance, reconciliation, or earnings report submitted by Transmission Owner to 
the NY PSC under the NY PSC Rate Order, to the extent such filing reports actual 
T/D plant balances, expenses, or other inputs for the most recently completed 
reporting period; and 
(iii) to the extent an input is not separately stated in the sources identified in clauses 
(i) and (ii) above, Transmission Owner’s books and records maintained in the 
ordinary course of business in accordance with the uniform system of accounts 
prescribed by the NY PSC for electric corporations and, to the extent consistent 
therewith, FERC’s Uniform System of Accounts, 18 C.F.R. Part 101, and the 
functionalization and allocation methodologies employed in the NY PSC Rate 
Order. 
(iv) If an input required by this Section 5 is not stated in, or cannot be derived from, 
the sources identified in clauses (i) through (iii) above for the applicable reporting 
period, Transmission Owner shall derive such input from its most recent FERC 
Form No. 1, using the functionalization and allocation methodologies employed in 
the NY PSC Rate Order, and shall identify such input in the informational statement 
provided under Section 6(d) of this Appendix B. 
The incorporation of NY PSC-approved inputs in this Section 5 is solely for the purpose 
of measuring the annual carrying cost of the Identified Upgrades under this Agreement, 
and the Rate Data Sources are incorporated solely as inputs to the formula set forth in this 
Appendix B. Such incorporation shall not (A) constitute a waiver or limitation of FERC’s 
jurisdiction over the rates, terms, and conditions of this Agreement under Sections 205 and 
206 of the FPA, as reserved in Section 9.2 of the Agreement, or (B) constitute an assertion 
of FERC jurisdiction over any retail rate established by the NY PSC, in each case subject 
to Article 2 of the Agreement. A change to an input resulting from a NY PSC order issued 
after the effective date of this Agreement shall be implemented through the annual update 
under Section 6 of this Appendix B and shall not require a filing with FERC under Section 
205 of the FPA, unless such change modifies the formula set forth in this Appendix B. All 
inputs shall be drawn from the same reporting period and functionalized on a consistent 
basis. Customer may challenge the computation or application of any input in accordance 
with Section 6(d) of this Appendix B and Section 9.11 of the Agreement; provided that the 
reasonableness of any input approved by the NY PSC in the NY PSC Rate Order shall not 
be subject to challenge under this Agreement. 
(c) Total T/D Plant (Denominator). Total T/D Plant shall equal the sum of the following, 
each stated at gross original cost before deduction of accumulated depreciation and 
amortization, and limited to plant in service: 
(i) T/D Plant, consisting of transmission plant in service and distribution plant in 
service, as recorded in the applicable transmission and distribution plant accounts

of the Uniform System of Accounts and reported in Transmission Owner’s FERC 
Form No. 1; and 
(ii) T/D Related Intangible and General Plant, consisting of intangible plant and 
general plant functionalized to the transmission and distribution functions using the 
allocation factors employed in the Rate Data Sources. 
(d) Total T/D Investment Base. The Total T/D Investment Base, which forms the basis 
for the return component described in Section 5(e)(i) of this Appendix B, shall be 
determined as follows: 
(i) Net Investment, equal to Total T/D Plant, less the T/D related accumulated 
provision for depreciation and amortization, less the T/D related accumulated 
deferred income taxes (net of associated deferred tax assets), and plus or minus 
other regulatory assets and regulatory liabilities includable in rate base under the 
Rate Data Sources; plus 
(ii) T/D Prepayments (Account 165) and T/D Materials and Supplies (Account 
154), each as functionalized to the transmission and distribution functions; less 
(iii) T/D Related Cash Working Capital, determined in accordance with the cash 
working capital methodology employed in the Rate Data Sources. 
(e) Total T/D Revenue Requirements Allocable (Numerator). Total T/D Revenue 
Requirements Allocable shall equal the sum of the following components, each 
functionalized to the transmission and distribution functions in accordance with the Rate 
Data Sources: 
(i) Return and Associated Income Taxes, equal to the Total T/D Investment Base 
multiplied by Transmission Owner’s weighted average cost of capital, reflecting 
the capital structure, embedded cost of long-term debt, cost of preferred stock (if 
any), and return on common equity most recently approved or accepted for 
Transmission Owner by the NY PSC, grossed up for federal and state income taxes 
at the applicable statutory rates; 
(ii) T/D Depreciation and Amortization Expense, equal to the depreciation and 
amortization expense recorded for T/D Plant and T/D Related Intangible and 
General Plant, calculated using the depreciation rates most recently approved or 
accepted for Transmission Owner by the applicable regulatory authority; 
(iii) T/D Related Municipal Tax Expense, equal to the real property and other 
municipal taxes recorded as taxes other than income taxes (Account 408.1) and 
attributable to the transmission and distribution functions; 
(iv) T/D Related Payroll Tax Expense, equal to the payroll taxes recorded as taxes 
other than income taxes (Account 408.1) and allocated to the transmission and 
distribution functions; 
(v) T/D Operation and Maintenance Expense, equal to the transmission and 
distribution operation and maintenance expenses recorded in the applicable 
expense accounts of the Uniform System of Accounts, [excluding any costs 
recovered through separately stated surcharges, pass-through mechanisms, or 
NYISO charges];

(vi) T/D Related Administrative and General Expense, equal to administrative 
and general expenses (Accounts 920 through 935) allocated to the transmission and 
distribution functions, excluding any items excluded from recovery under the Rate 
Data Sources; less 
(vii) T/D Rents Received from Electric Property, equal to rents from electric 
property (Account 454) attributable to the transmission and distribution functions, 
which shall be applied as a reduction to the revenue requirement; provided that 
revenues received by Transmission Owner under this Agreement shall be excluded 
from this component. 
6. Annual Update and True-Up 
(a) Annual Update. No later than August 1 of each calendar year during the Contract Term 
and the year immediately following the Contract Term, Transmission Owner shall 
recalculate the Large Load Upgrade-Specific Capital Revenue Requirement and Annual 
On-going Charge Factor using the Rate Data Sources then most recently available, and 
shall recalculate the Estimated Annual Revenue Requirement, the Estimated Accelerated 
Annual Revenue Requirement, the Annual Deferred Revenue, and the monthly Large Load 
Upgrade Charge for the succeeding Billing Year in accordance with Sections 3 and 5 of 
this Appendix B. Each annual update shall reflect, without limitation, changes during the 
Contract Term in Transmission Owner’s approved or accepted return on common equity 
and depreciation rates.  
(b) Annual True-Up. Because the Annual On-going Charge Factor applied in each Billing 
Year is derived from data for the most recently completed reporting year, the Large Load 
Upgrade Charge billed for each Billing Year shall be an estimate. In the Billing Year 
following each Billing Year, Transmission Owner shall determine the difference between 
(i) the Large Load Upgrade Charge billed for the prior Billing Year and (ii) the Large Load 
Upgrade Charge that would have been billed for that Billing Year using the Annual On-
going Charge Factor, the Large Load Upgrade-Specific Capital Revenue Requirement, and 
Large Load Upgrade Gross Plant in Service derived from actual data for the corresponding 
period. Any resulting over-recovery or under-recovery, together with interest calculated in 
accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 35.19a, shall be refunded to or surcharged to Customer, as 
applicable, in equal monthly installments over the succeeding Billing Year, in accordance 
with the accounting protocols set forth in Appendix C. 
(c) Replacement of Estimated Costs. Upon completion of the Final Cost Reconciliation 
Protocol set forth in Section 1 of Appendix C, the actual Reimbursable Costs of each 
Identified Upgrade shall replace the Estimated Network Upgrade Book Value for all 
purposes of this Appendix B. Transmission Owner shall recalculate the Large Load 
Upgrade Charge prospectively and shall true up all amounts billed from the 
Commencement Date, with interest calculated in accordance with 18 C.F.R. § 35.19a. 
(d) Informational Statement. Concurrently with each annual update, Transmission 
Owner shall provide Customer with a written statement setting forth the recalculated 
Annual On-going Charge Factor, Large Load Upgrade-Specific Capital Revenue 
Requirement, and Large Load Upgrade Gross Plant in Service, and each input used to 
determine those amounts, the specific Rate Data Source and account or line reference from

which each input was derived, the true-up calculation for the prior Billing Year, and the 
revised schedule under Section 4 of this Appendix B, together with supporting workpapers. 
Transmission Owner may use such statement to satisfy any reporting or posting obligations 
under the NYISO OATT or applicable FERC or NY PSC requirements. Customer may 
review and challenge any annual update in accordance with Section 9.11 of the Agreement. 
(e) Expiration of Contract Term. Following the final annual true-up for the last Billing 
Year of the Contract Term, no further updates or true-ups of the Large Load Upgrade 
Charge shall be performed under this Agreement. Any over-recovery or under-recovery 
attributable to changes in the inputs to the Annual On-going Charge Factor occurring in 
the year after the expiration of the Contract Term shall be addressed in Transmission 
Owner’s rate proceedings before FERC or the NY PSC, as applicable, and shall not be 
billed to or refunded to Customer. 
(f) No Double Recovery. Nothing in this Appendix B shall permit Transmission Owner to 
recover, through FERC-jurisdictional wholesale transmission rates or NY PSC-
jurisdictional retail delivery rates, any revenue requirement associated with the Identified 
Upgrades that has been recovered from Customer under this Agreement, consistent with 
the NYISO OATT. 
(g) Early Termination. In the event of termination prior to the expiration of the Assessment 
Period, the Net Present Value Residual Charge under Section 4.3 of the Agreement shall be 
calculated net of the accumulated Annual Deferred Revenue collected from Customer through 
the date of termination. 
 
7. TO Attachment Facilities Cost Recovery Special Provisions 
 
Any alternative cost recovery arrangement for the TO Attachment Facilities agreed to by the 
Parties shall be set forth in this Section 7 and shall, at a minimum, specify: (i) the capital 
payment amount and schedule; (ii) the exclusion of amounts so paid from the revenue 
requirement and the Large Load Upgrade Charge; (iii) the income tax treatment, including any 
gross-up and true-up; (iv) the treatment of operation, maintenance, repair and replacement costs 
during and after the Term; (v) any resulting adjustments to security under the Large Load 
Security Agreement; and (vi) treatment upon termination. Transmission Owner shall make any 
such arrangement available on a non-discriminatory basis to similarly situated customers. If the 
Parties exercise their rights under this Section 7, Transmission Owner shall file this Agreement, 
or any amendment under Section 9.6 adding or changing this Section 7, with FERC, and such 
terms shall not take effect until accepted by FERC. If FERC does not accept such terms, the 
default treatment under Section 4.4 shall apply.

APPENDIX C: TRUE-UP AND ANNUAL REVENUE 
CREDITING ACCOUNTING PROTOCOLS 
1. Final Cost Reconciliation Protocol 
(a) Within one hundred eighty (180) days after the COD, Transmission Owner shall 
assemble all direct work orders, material invoices, internal payroll overheads, and 
AFUDC computations recorded in accordance with FERC’s Uniform System of 
Accounts (18 C.F.R. Part 101) and NY PSC accounting guidelines. 
(b) A formal accounting statement detailing any variance between the preliminary 
estimates in Appendix B and actual Reimbursable Costs will be submitted to Customer 
and NY PSC Staff. 
(c) Billing adjustments or refunds shall be processed within thirty (30) days thereafter. 
2. Revenue Crediting and Prevention of Cost Shifting 
(a) Revenue Crediting: All funds collected from Customer toward the carrying charges or 
capital costs of the Identified Upgrades shall be credited or otherwise reflected in 
Transmission Owner’s applicable wholesale transmission revenue requirement or retail 
rate base, as appropriate, consistent with Article 2 and the NYISO OATT, so that non-
participating wholesale and retail customers are insulated from the capital and operating 
costs of the dedicated Identified Upgrades.
